findings.comment: Indicate on the electrical plan that all meter locations are within sight of an Austin Energy transformer. Include sight-line notation or written confirmation on the plan for each meter-to-transformer relationship.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows eight meters on building exterior walls and four transformers at various site locations. Vision analysis confirms: 'Meter locations are marked by small grouped rectangles on the building exteriors and are explicitly labeled "Electrical Meters" with leader lines pointing to them. There is no text, notation, or graphic indicating a required line of sight to the transformers.' The grouping guidance notes: 'current code requires "within sight" visibility but does not specify a maximum distance—older references to "150 ft line of sight" are not codified in current UCM.'
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.9.3.1.B, all meter locations must be 'within sight of an Austin Energy transformer.' From a 2D site plan view, it is difficult to definitively determine whether meters on building walls can see transformers located elsewhere on the site without 3D visualization or explicit line-of-sight notations. The site plan does not include sight-line annotations, distance measurements, or clear notation confirming that each meter location is within sight of at least one transformer. This creates ambiguity about compliance.

findings.comment: Meter sight line to transformer not verified. Show on the electrical plan or a separate diagram that each electrical meter is within clear sight line of its serving transformer. If any meter does not have direct line of sight to the nearest transformer, provide written approval from Austin Energy Design and Distribution Metering business units for the exception. Provide sight line diagrams or cross-reference elevation views confirming visibility.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meter locations on building exterior walls and 4 transformer pad locations distributed across the site. Meters appear to be positioned on various building sides (north, west, south, east). Transformers are located in northwest, southwest, northeast, and southeast areas. Without clear sight line diagrams, elevation views, or explicit distance callouts, it is not possible to verify that all 8 meters are within sight of an Austin Energy transformer. The term "within sight" in UCM § 1.9.3.1.B does not specify a distance limit (older references to "150 ft line of sight" are not codified), but direct visual contact must be apparent. Given the distributed meter and transformer locations, several meters may not have clear line-of-sight to a transformer.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1.B requires meters to be within sight of an Austin Energy transformer. The grouping notes that "within sight" visibility is the current code requirement with no maximum distance specified, but direct visual contact is required. Without sight line diagrams showing clear, unobstructed lines between each meter and its serving transformer, the reviewer cannot confirm compliance. The scattered distribution of transformers and meters across 8 buildings suggests that some meters may be obstructed by building walls or other structures, requiring line-of-sight verification or AE Design approval for exceptions.

findings.comment: Whether electric line extension is required cannot be determined from the site plan alone. This determination must be made by Austin Energy Design based on existing infrastructure capacity and location. Provide Austin Energy ESPA approval documentation, Letter of Agreement for Underground Electric Service, or utility coordination notes confirming whether line extension is required and any associated costs or conditions.
findings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows underground electric line routing entering the site from Valley View Road on the west side, but does not include any notation indicating whether a line extension from Austin Energy's existing infrastructure is required. The supplementary documents (Master Comment Report referencing Austin Energy Design Criteria, Bluebeam link to AE comments) suggest that Austin Energy has reviewed the project, but the specific comments regarding line extension determination are not accessible in the available documents. The grouping definition explicitly states that 'whether line extension is required (vs. Service-Only service) cannot be determined from site plan features alone - this determination is made by AE Design based on existing infrastructure capacity and location.'
findings.reasoning: Per the grouping definition, 'Line extension' determination cannot be made from site plan analysis alone and requires 'Austin Energy ESPA approval letters, Letter of Agreement for Underground Electric Service, or utility coordination notes stating line extension requirement and costs.' The presence of underground line routing on Sheet 21 could indicate either a service-only installation (connecting to existing nearby AE infrastructure) or a line extension (new AE infrastructure required). Without AE Design documentation (ESPA, Letter of Agreement, or utility coordination notes), the status cannot be definitively determined. The applicant must provide AE Design determination documentation.

findings.comment: Cannot verify whether electric line extension is required from available evidence. Provide Austin Energy ESPA approval letter or Letter of Agreement for Underground Electric Service confirming whether line extension is required and, if so, showing the extent of the line extension on the electrical design plan per UCM § 1.3.12 and UCM § 1.16.0(6).
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric service routing from the existing right-of-way at Valley View Road to the site, with connection to transformer pads and building meter locations. However, no documentation indicates whether this represents a "Line Extension" (customer-paid infrastructure extension to reach the site) or a "Service-Only" connection to existing nearby infrastructure. No terms such as "line extension," "CIAC" (Contribution in Aid of Construction), or "service-only" appear on the plans. The Master Comment Report's Electric Review section references Austin Energy Design Criteria but the actual AE Design determination (via ESPA approval or Letter of Agreement) is not provided in the project file.
findings.reasoning: The grouping's regulatory overview states: "Whether line extension is required (vs. Service-Only service) cannot be determined from site plan features alone - this determination is made by AE Design based on existing infrastructure capacity and location." The checklist item applicability note directs reviewers to: "Check: Austin Energy ESPA approval letters, Letter of Agreement for Underground Electric Service, or utility coordination notes stating line extension requirement and costs." The absence of this critical AE Design documentation means line extension applicability cannot be verified from available evidence.

findings.comment: If Austin Energy Design requires switchgear for this multi-transformer configuration, show the switchgear location on Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan). Provide documentation of Austin Energy coordination confirming whether switchgear is required. If switchgear is not required, note this in the electrical specifications.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 5 transformer pads serving 8 buildings. The applicability note states: 'Only when two or more transformers proposed or otherwise required per Austin Energy Design. Check: transformer count on plans or Austin Energy requirements letter.' Five transformers are proposed, which appears to meet the threshold of 'two or more.' However, the note also requires 'AE Design coordination to determine applicability' for switchgear location. No switchgear location is shown on the plans, and no documentation indicates whether Austin Energy Design has specified a switchgear requirement for this configuration.
findings.reasoning: Switchgear may or may not be required depending on Austin Energy's specific design for this project. The plans do not indicate whether switchgear is part of the approved electrical design. Without explicit Austin Energy Design coordination documentation, the applicability of this switchgear requirement cannot be confirmed.

findings.comment: Switchgear applicability to this project not verified. Provide load calculations confirming whether switchgear is required. If switchgear is needed, provide evidence of coordination with Austin Energy Design lead.
findings.observation: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows transformers and electrical equipment routing but does not specifically indicate whether switchgear is required or shown on the plans. No load calculations or correspondence indicating switchgear requirement was found in the documentation. Switchgear is typically required only for very high loads (generally >1000 kVA or complex multi-service installations), which may not apply to this 39-unit residential development.
findings.reasoning: Switchgear installation requires coordination with Austin Energy design lead only when high electrical loads require switchgear per UCM § 1.16.0(6). For a 39-unit townhome project, switchgear is likely not required (typical residential loads are served by standard service transformers and panels). However, without load calculations showing the total project demand, the applicability of this requirement cannot be definitively determined. If load calculations show switchgear is not needed, this item would be n/a.

findings.comment: Confirm with Austin Energy Design whether switchgear is required for the four-transformer configuration. If switchgear is required, show its location and integrate it into the electrical plan with proper labeling and coordination notes.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformers but does not show a switchgear, load centers, or transmission interconnects linking the transformers. The grouping guidance states: 'Switchgear location not shown when required based on electrical service configuration' and 'Requires AE Design coordination to determine applicability.' With multiple transformers (four) proposed, it is unclear whether they are configured as independent service points or as a coordinated system requiring switchgear.
findings.reasoning: Per Reviewer Convention, when two or more transformers are proposed, Austin Energy may require switchgear for coordination and switching capability. The necessity of switchgear is determined during Austin Energy Design coordination. Without evidence of this coordination or a documented Austin Energy requirements letter, it cannot be determined whether switchgear is required and whether its location must be shown on plans.

findings.comment: If dual feed electricity service is being requested, provide electrical load calculations, service configuration details on the electrical site plan, and Austin Energy approval letter specifically addressing dual feed service per UCM § 1.5.2.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows what appears to be a single electrical service configuration with four transformer pads serving the 39 townhome units. No dual feed electrical service is mentioned in the electrical design, electrical load calculations, or on any plan sheets. No Austin Energy approval letter specifically addressing dual feed is present in the submitted documentation. The grouping states applicability is 'Only when dual feed service is requested,' which appears not to be the case based on the preliminary design shown.
findings.reasoning: Dual feed service is a specialized configuration where a site receives power from two separate Austin Energy service points. This is typically requested for large commercial or critical facilities requiring redundancy. The preliminary electrical design shown on Sheet 21 does not indicate a dual feed configuration. Without evidence of a dual feed request, this item appears not applicable. However, the final determination cannot be confirmed without Austin Energy ESPA documentation.

findings.comment: Obtain and provide Austin Energy's Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) approval letter which contains the determination of whether line extension is required to serve the site, and if required, documentation of Contributions in Aid of Construction (CIAC) or line extension fees per UCM § 1.3.12.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows proposed transformer pads and underground service routing to the buildings. No plan notes reference line extension, Contributions in Aid of Construction (CIAC), line extension fees, or any line extension requirements. The grouping states that line extension determination 'cannot be determined from site plans alone' and 'is made exclusively by Austin Energy during the Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) review process.' No ESPA approval documentation is provided in the submitted plans or supplementary documents. The Master Comment Report confirms 'AE completeness check complete' but the actual ESPA letter with line extension determination is not provided.
findings.reasoning: Whether a line extension is required to serve the site is a technical determination made exclusively by Austin Energy during ESPA review based on existing infrastructure capacity and location. This determination is not visible in the site plan documents. Without the ESPA documentation that contains Austin Energy's line extension determination, the applicability cannot be confirmed. The preliminary electrical design assumes service is available, but whether extension of existing infrastructure is required remains undetermined.

findings.comment: Confirm in writing that the site at 3759 Valley View Road is within Austin Energy's service territory. If confirmed, ensure all Austin Energy standards and references remain on plans. If outside service territory, remove all Austin Energy references and notes from plans.
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) includes Site Plan Release Note item (e) stating 'Water and wastewater service will be provided by the City of Austin (or identify the service provider if other than the City of Austin).' This phrasing indicates the service provider for water/wastewater may not be confirmed as City of Austin. However, the equivalent note for electrical service is not explicit on the plans. The site location is in Austin city limits (jurisdiction confirmed as 'City of Austin — Full Purpose'), but specific verification that the site is within Austin Energy's electrical service territory is not documented on the plans or in supplementary documents. Without explicit confirmation of Austin Energy service territory inclusion, compliance with Code of Ordinances § 15-9-1 cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: Code of Ordinances § 15-9-1 establishes service territory boundaries. Sites outside Austin Energy's service territory must have all Austin Energy references and notes removed from plans. Conversely, sites within the territory must maintain appropriate Austin Energy references. The grouping requires 'site location relative to Austin Energy service boundaries' and states 'if outside AE territory, plans should not reference AE standards.' The submission contains multiple Austin Energy design criteria references (Sheet 3 transmission clearances, Master Comment Report electric review), which implies territory inclusion, but explicit confirmation is not provided.

findings.comment: Determine whether the site is in a dual service area between Austin Energy and another utility provider. If so, and if non-territorial service is requested, complete and submit the Public Utility Commission Service Area Exception Application per Texas Public Utility Regulatory Act.
codeCitations: Texas Public Utility Regulatory Act (state law)
applicableAreas: Service provider selection in dual territory areas
findings.observation: No documentation is provided indicating whether the site is located in a dual service area where both Austin Energy and another utility provider operate. No Public Utility Commission Service Area Exception Application or service provider selection documentation is present in the submitted materials. The grouping states applicability is 'Only when development is in dual service area between Austin Energy and another provider AND requests service from non-territorial provider.' No evidence of this scenario is apparent from the site plan documents or supplementary files.
findings.reasoning: PUC Service Area Exception Applications are required only when a customer in a dual service area (where both Austin Energy and another provider operate) requests service from the non-territorial provider. This is a state-level regulatory requirement under the Texas Public Utility Regulatory Act. The site location relative to dual service areas cannot be determined from site plan documents alone, and no service provider selection documentation is provided that would indicate this is applicable. The grouping explicitly requires 'Service territory maps, provider selection documentation, PUC application submittal' to assess this item.

findings.comment: Building electrical plans must clearly show the meter location and electrical service configuration, with explicit labeling of the boundary between Austin Energy-owned facilities (up to and including meter) and customer-owned facilities (load side of meter). Customer-owned conduit and cable are under City Electrical Inspector jurisdiction and should not be submitted for Austin Energy approval. This determination cannot be made from site plan review alone; verification is required during building plan stage.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) at the site plan stage shows only a high-level service routing diagram with transformer locations, underground line routing, pull boxes, and meters. The distinction between Austin Energy-owned infrastructure (up to meter) and customer-owned infrastructure (from meter/load side) is not explicitly shown or labeled on the site plan. The specific identification of customer-owned conduit and cable on the load side of the meter typically requires building electrical plans with detailed electrical room design and service panel locations. The grouping states applicability is 'Only when customer-owned conduit and cable on load side of meter is proposed' and requires 'Electrical service design, meter location, ownership boundaries; customer-owned facilities beyond meter point are under City Electrical Inspector jurisdiction, not Austin Energy.'
findings.reasoning: This deficiency addresses a jurisdictional issue: customer-owned facilities beyond the meter point fall under City of Austin Building/Electrical Inspector jurisdiction, not Austin Energy jurisdiction. The site plan documents do not show the interior building electrical design or meter room configuration that would clarify where the meter is located and what facilities are customer-owned. This determination requires building electrical plans rather than site plan review. However, to avoid future confusion, the site plan should either clarify this boundary or the building plans must show the proper jurisdictional delineation.

findings.comment: Electrical room design and exterior door access requirements will be verified during building plan review per Austin Energy requirements under UCM Section 1. Building electrical plans must show each electrical room with an exterior-accessible door for Austin Energy service access, proper clearances, ventilation, and fire-rated walls as required.
findings.observation: The Site Plan (Sheet 9) provides overall site layout and building footprints for eight multi-unit townhome buildings. Visual analysis of the site plan found 'no rooms within the building footprints labeled as electrical rooms' and 'no doors explicitly labeled or marked as electrical room doors on any of the buildings.' The interior building electrical room design and door configuration are architectural/building plan elements not typically depicted on site plans. The grouping states applicability is 'Only when electrical room is provided in building' and requires 'Building plans, electrical room design, exterior access per Austin Energy requirements.' These details are documented on building electrical plans, not site plans.
findings.reasoning: Electrical room exterior door requirements are specified in Austin Energy design standards (UCM Section 1) to ensure that Austin Energy service personnel can access metering and service equipment without entering tenant-occupied spaces. This is a building-level design requirement verified during building plan review, not a site plan-level requirement. The site plan review stage does not typically include verification of interior building room configurations or door placements. This deficiency should be assessed during building electrical plan review with the City Electrical Inspector and Austin Energy reviewers.
